page: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a dedicated general purpose cloud server driven by the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor family. The instance is provisioned with 48 dedicated virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by standard hardware extensions including AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2 under a QEMU hypervisor.

The virtual machine includes 188.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of roughly 3.91 GB per vCPU, which aligns closely with balanced general-purpose profiles. Primary storage is bundled directly with a 960 GB local NVMe SSD. The instance does not feature dedicated graphics processing hardware and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on IPv6 or external networking configurations.

Benchmark assessments show substantial compute and parallel processing throughput. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves top-quartile results across both single-core (3044.99) and multi-core (73209.23) metrics. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 reached 305.9 GB/sec, while PassMark tests recorded 64305.59 for CPU computation and 22243.57 for database operations. Workloads involving in-memory key-value processing demonstrated 62.09 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. Software compilation benchmarks with Clang similarly placed in the upper quartile.

Resource scaling tradeoffs center on the architecture clock rate and memory subsystems. Memory bandwidth on uncached block tests operates in the middle 50% percentile (148.56 GB/sec read, 80.13 GB/sec write), and AVX-512 instructions are unsupported. Consequently, while unsuitable for advanced vector matrix processing or GPU tasks, Hetzner Cloud ccx63 functions efficiently for highly concurrent microservices, CI/CD compilation pipelines, enterprise database hosting, and large-scale Redis deployments.
description: Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is a general purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor offering 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores at 2.0 GHz. The system provides 188.0 GB of RAM, equating to approximately 3.91 GB per vCPU, and includes 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware accelerators are absent. Benchmark evaluations indicate top-quartile multi-core processing in stress-ng and strong execution across database operations and Clang compilation tasks, accompanied by 62.09 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. While memory bandwidth and single-thread throughput fall within standard median tiers and AVX-512 is unsupported, the predictable dedicated CPU allocation delivers stable resource density. Hetzner Cloud ccx63 is strategically matched for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, transactional databases, high-throughput caching, and general compute-heavy enterprise backends.
